feature: Retroactive LOINC unification at display time (Dosar medical, Comparatii, Grafice/Evolutie)
test_type: static + .NET console probe (/tmp/uniprobe) against real code paths
build: dotnet build MedicalApp.csproj => Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)
checks: LoincUnifier.Analyze remaps 2093-3 -> 14647-2 when name+unit+range identical (anchor beats semantic)
Ferritin with missing unit on one report is NOT merged (prudent rule) and is flagged MissingAxis=unit
Limfocite % (736-9) vs absolute (731-0) never merged (unit+range differ) and NO warning raised
Compare: unified analyte collapses from 2 rows to 1, both cells present, long name follows the winning code, drift warning gone
Compare: non-unifiable rows keep 2 rows + MissingAxis=unit
Dossier: unified analyte becomes ONE card with a 2-entry timeline and trend=up on the newer entry
Dossier: non-unifiable analyte keeps 2 cards flagged MissingAxis=unit
Loc.cs: LoincUnifyMissingUnitTip / RangeTip / BothTip present and non-empty in all 7 languages (21 keys)
bug_found_and_fixed: LoincUnifier.NormalizeRange treated the range separator '-' as a minus sign, so "0-200" produced [0,-200] and "0 - 200" produced [0,200] => identical ranges never matched and NOTHING was ever unified. Dashes are now stripped as separators before number extraction.
not_covered_by_automated_test: BuildEvolutionAsync (requires a live SQL Server); it uses the same LoincUnifier.Unify map (verified in isolation) to resolve both the stored codes and the codes the user pastes.
db_migrations: none - display-only change, DB schema untouched
